page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (specifically AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 7 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the ecs.c8a.4xlarge demonstrates strong single-core performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core evaluations. Text processing performance is also strong. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff: while cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is average at 1216.18 GB/sec, uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, measuring 36.9 GB/sec and placing in the bottom 25%. Other operations, such as Redis SET commands, static web serving throughput, and software compilation, consistently register average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dedicated compute profile with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The presence of AVX-512 instructions provides efficient processing for vector calculations and cryptography without the premium of GPU hardware. Given these characteristics, the ecs.c8a.4xlarge is suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations.
